Max Margin Interval Tree Changepoint Learner

Source: R/LearnerCptMMIT.R
mlr_learners_changepoint.mmit.Rd

Learns a penalty function for changepoint detection from weak labels via a max margin interval tree, mmit::mmit().

At train time, each sequence is summarized into a numeric feature vector and the labels are converted into an interval of admissible log(lambda) penalties (the segment path is fitted per sequence, scored against the label regions, and the error curve inverted). The tree fits these interval targets directly with a hinge loss, so unlike mlr_learners_changepoint.intregrcv it also trains when no label gives a finite lower (or upper) penalty limit.

At predict time, the learner returns response, the predicted log(lambda) per sequence.

The label solvers are chosen by the task's label_type: "changepoint" uses changepoint::cpt.mean(), "peak" uses PeakSegOptimal::PeakSegPDPAchrom().

The 'mmit' package is not on CRAN. The upstream sources no longer compile with current C++ toolchains on macOS and Windows, so install the patched copy with pak::pak("sleepysnorlax05/mmit/Rpackage").

Dictionary

This learner can be retrieved via mlr3::mlr_learners with the key "changepoint.mmit":

lrn("changepoint.mmit")

Parameters

Kmax (integer(1), required) caps model complexity: the maximum number of changepoints (label_type = "changepoint") or peaks (label_type = "peak") the per-sequence segment path is searched over. The learner uses it to build the target penalty intervals at train time and does not forward it to the solver. Each prediction records it per sequence in its extra data (as.data.table(prediction)$Kmax), so the label-error measure decodes the predicted penalty under the same cap.

max_depth (integer(1), default Inf for unlimited depth) and margin are passed to mmit::mmit(); see there for their meaning. Its loss and min_sample arguments are not exposed: mmit() does not forward them to the tree builder, so they change neither the fitted tree nor its predictions.

Examples

library(data.table)

set.seed(36)
signal = vector("list", 10L)
label = vector("list", 10L)
for (i in 1:10) {
  if (i %% 2 == 1) {
    signal[[i]] = c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9))
    label[[i]] = data.table(
      start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = c("1change", "1change")
    )
  } else {
    signal[[i]] = rnorm(100, 0)
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  }
}
task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = data.table(signal = signal, label = label),
  target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
)

learner = lrn("changepoint.mmit", Kmax = 3L)
# \donttest{
learner$train(task)
learner$predict(task)
#> 
#> ── <PredictionCpt> for 10 observations: ────────────────────────────────────────
#>  row_ids             truth response Kmax
#>        1 <data.table[2x3]> 6.147529    3
#>        2 <data.table[1x3]> 6.147529    3
#>        3 <data.table[2x3]> 6.147529    3
#>      ---               ---      ---  ---
#>        8 <data.table[1x3]> 6.147529    3
#>        9 <data.table[2x3]> 6.147529    3
#>       10 <data.table[1x3]> 6.147529    3
# }
